attempt: Row 1: Original baseline (fixed 3 features, not re-derived per fold)
verdict: Reference result as originally reported. NOTE: feature list was fixed (chosen once from an earlier age-regression analysis, never re-derived against the classification target) -- not a fully nested/honest baseline.

attempt: Row 2: Corrected baseline (nested top-3 vs GROUP, per fold)
verdict: Far worse than Row 1 (Wilcoxon vs Row1 p=0.0023). Selecting features against 'group' directly, per fold, performs worse than chance -- an unexpected and important negative finding, not adopted as the working baseline.

attempt: Row 2b: Corrected baseline (nested top-3 vs AGE, per fold) -- TRUE baseline for Improvements 1-5
verdict: Worse than Row 1 (Wilcoxon vs Row1 p=0.0455) but the only methodologically honest per-fold-reselected reference point (features re-derived from training fold only, against age, matching how the original 3 features were originally chosen). Used as the comparison baseline for all Improvements below. Permutation test not run (not the primary result; superseded by testing whether any improvement beats it).

attempt: Improvement 1: Up to 5 features, threshold |rho|>0.3 (nested per fold)
verdict: No improvement in accuracy over Row 2b; AUC worse. Not significant vs Row 2b. Not confirmed.
Accuracy and AUC both nominally higher than Row 2b, but difference not significant (Wilcoxon p=0.2568). Not confirmed.

attempt: Improvement 3: C grid search via inner LOOCV (nested top-3 vs age)
verdict: No improvement over Row 2b. Permutation test skipped (231 min estimated cost, no positive signal to justify it).

attempt: Improvement 4: Decision threshold tuned via inner LOOCV (nested top-3 vs age)
verdict: Highest raw accuracy among the per-fold-reselected configurations, but AUC unchanged from Row 2b and not significant vs Row 2b (p=0.1797). Gain driven by sensitivity/specificity imbalance (predicts 'old' far more often), not by genuine improved discrimination. Not confirmed.

attempt: Improvement 5: class_weight='balanced' + threshold tuning combined (nested top-3 vs age)
verdict: Accuracy matches Row 1 numerically, and is statistically indistinguishable from Row 1 (Wilcoxon vs Row1 p=1.0000) -- but NOT significantly better than Row 2b either (p=0.1025), and AUC (0.5481) remains well below Row 1's AUC (0.6779). The gain comes almost entirely from very high sensitivity (0.9231) and low specificity (0.3750), i.e. predicting 'old' for most participants, not from better discrimination. CONFIRMED NOT SIGNIFICANT: 500-shuffle permutation test gives p=0.3120 -- an AUC of 0.5481 or higher occurs in 31% of random label shuffles, i.e. indistinguishable from chance. Improvement 5 is REJECTED as a real improvement.
